title: Closed proper base change on bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs over a qcqs base
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure, and an admissible commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$: a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, or $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E$, with exactly the discrete or induced $\ell$-adic topological condensed-ring convention of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$, the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the finite constant scalar-model constructibility and finite Tor amplitude of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Let $S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, $q:Y\to S$ proper and $f:X\to Y$ proper, and $c:C\hookrightarrow Y$ a closed immersion whose complementary open immersion is quasi-compact [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Form $X_C=X\times_Y C$, with projections $a:X_C\to X$ and $f_C:X_C\to C$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every $L\in\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda)$ the canonical ambient exchange map [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]
$$c^*Rf_*L\longrightarrow R(f_C)_*a^*L$$
is an isomorphism in $D_C$. Pullback means the exact module inverse image with the pulled-back coefficient rings. There is no field, characteristic, Noetherian, finite-dimensional-base, or density hypothesis.

proof.text: The canonical ambient exchange is a shift-compatible transformation between triangulated functors. Its isomorphism locus is replete and triangulated. Constructibility is invariant under isomorphism by the existing proved private theorem AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.constructible_iso, imported using import all from Sheaf.Paper.IndConstructibleFilteredColimits; it transports the finite scalar models along the stratum and covering inverse images. Apply DerivedCategory.prop_of_bounded from the proved source-library TStructure module: finite Postnikov induction using truncation triangles and triangle two-out-of-three extends invertibility from constructible sheaves in degree zero to every bounded complex with constructible cohomology. The finite Tor condition on the given L is not required by this induction.

The statement is byte-identical to the base, and the Q̄_ℓ = C(−,Q̄_ℓ) convention is kept. Each old step has a carrier: old 1 → A (closed-pullback/Tor) + B (finite witness and normalized mate); old 2 → A (completion via Roos cone); old 4 → C (two-transpose rectangle); old 5 → D (shifts). Old 3 and old 6 were already citation assemblies and stay as item steps 2 and 3. Step 3 now uses the generator and scalar nodes only in their finite-E clauses. New step 4 handles C(−,Q̄_ℓ) and is sound. F (true, since the affine-source proof never uses affineness of X) gives tests W=Spec B, V=Spec(B/IB) with IB ⊆ Jac B, so Jac(B/IB)=Jac(B)/IB and V and W have the same closed-point quotient. Rigidity applied to f_U at W and to f_Z at V, then 2-out-of-3, makes the test restriction invertible on each module in P. Truncation extends this to bounded L, and F's detection finishes.
